newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen firm, red chip index to make debut.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen firm, red chip index to make debut.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are set for a firm session on Monday, recovering from a slump in prices last week and benefiting from the launch of a new China-linked index which should boost sentiment and interest in red chip stocks.
"There will be continued recovery this week," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

"Investors are expecting quite a good performance during the handover period and the new China index will have a positive impact on the red chips since investors are still bullish about Chinese economic prospects," he said.
The Hang Seng Index closed at 14,112.55 points on Friday.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London gained 102.60 points to 14,215.15.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said continued concerns about possible government measures to cool down the property market would limit any gains on Monday.
"The market will move sideways due to uncertainty about the property market although it may open higher," he said.
"But the red chips will be quite interesting today."
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index stood at 2,490.20 points at the close of business on Thursday.
